## Minimum detectable effect: two figures, not a silent recomputation

Two MDE figures are reported side by side for every metric (D-32). `mde_two_sample_pct` is the authoritative figure: a two-sample current-versus-baseline comparison, `(Z_ALPHA_2 + Z_BETA) * sqrt(2 / n) * cv * 100`, carrying both a 95% confidence term and an 80% power term, because the gate itself compares a candidate run against a baseline. `mde_one_sample_provisional_pct` is Phase 1's provisional figure computed through the identical `perf_noise_report.provisional_mde` code path Phase 1's own report used: a one-sample confidence-interval half-width with no power term (`z * cv * 100 / sqrt(n)`), explicitly labelled provisional and non-binding in `NOISE-FLOOR-REPORT.md`'s "Provisional minimum detectable effect (non-binding)" section. The authoritative figure is larger than the provisional one by roughly a factor of two at this campaign's sample count: a threshold tuned against the provisional figure would have been tuned against an optimistic bound.

## Cross-CPU-model invariance

Every invariant-direction metric's invariance verdict is derived from an exact minimum-equals-maximum comparison applied per benchmark across every observed CPU model, with no tolerance, percentage band, or rounding step (D-31). Pooling every benchmark's samples into one list before comparing would make a metric collected on several benchmarks with legitimately differing counts unable to pass the bar however deterministic each individual benchmark's cell was, so the comparison is scoped to one benchmark at a time instead. A benchmark with fewer than 2 observed CPU models is not comparable and contributes nothing toward the verdict; a metric with no comparable benchmark at all reports `insufficient-samples` rather than a trivially-satisfied bit-identical verdict: one model demonstrates nothing about cross-model invariance. A metric the harness already demoted within a single run binds at Tier 2 regardless of what cross-model agreement would otherwise show (D-12). A metric whose registry direction is not invariant is never compared at all.

- CPU models observed by this campaign: 3 (AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor, INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C)

## Calibration flattening

Per candidate base metric and per calibration component: whether normalizing the raw metric by that component's own median measurably reduces across-host dispersion without inflating within-host dispersion (D-13). A pairing qualifies only when both hold; every pairing's figures are shown whether it qualifies or not, so a reader can see why. When no pairing qualifies for a metric, that is the finding (D-14): the normalized ratio stays published for trend value, marked non-gating, and host stratification of the baseline is named as the remedy that works instead.

| Base metric | Chosen pairing | Non-gating |
|---|---|---|
| cpu_process_ns_per_byte | n/a | True |
| cpu_process_ns_per_op | n/a | True |
| cpu_thread_ns_per_byte | n/a | True |
| cpu_thread_ns_per_op | n/a | True |

## Injected-load contamination

Per accepted run (including any run labelled `injected-load-demonstration`, which is excluded from every metrics/invariance/flattening figure above but shown here on purpose -- D-10): the count of rejected samples with their reasons, the count of metrics that reported INCONCLUSIVE with their reasons, and the tally of secondary steal/cgroup flags.

Rejection threshold derivations, quoted verbatim from `tests/perf/_perf_harness.py` so the report and the code cannot disagree:

- MAD band: band = median +/- DEFAULT_MAD_SIGMA_MULTIPLIER (3.0, the conventional three-sigma robust outlier bar) * MAD_SIGMA_SCALE (1.4826, the normal-consistency constant that converts a median absolute deviation into a standard-deviation estimate) * mad. A MAD of exactly zero collapses the band to exact equality: with every sibling identical, a differing sibling is genuinely anomalous, not a false positive.
- Steal delta: 659 measurement windows sampled in Phase 2's real campaign (docs/plans/perf-ci-hardening/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md, Steal time section), and every one recorded steal_jiffies_delta exactly zero (median 0, min 0, max 0, zero flagged against env_fingerprint's own >= 0.01 fractional threshold). Any nonzero delta observed by this harness therefore lies outside everything this runner fleet has ever shown, so the threshold here is 'nonzero', not a fraction calibrated against a distribution of nonzero values -- none exist yet to calibrate against. This campaign can therefore only report that no contention was observed; it cannot speak to gate behaviour under real steal, which stays untested.

This campaign observed no secondary steal or cgroup contention flag at all (D-11): the rejection path's behaviour under real steal is therefore untested, not validated.
